options.text: Using the highest heat setting and a large barrel, since fine hair resists curl

options.label: C
options.text: Using proper prep product, the right tool size, and a setting spray

options.label: D
options.text: Curling the hair while it is still damp so the curl forms faster

questions.correct_answer_text: Using proper prep product, the right tool size, and a setting spray
questions.explanation: Fine, straight hair often needs specific prep, a smaller barrel size, and a setting or hold product to help curls last, since it can otherwise fall out quickly.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a diffuser attachment on a blow dryer?

options.label: A
options.text: Spreading airflow gently, ideal for curly hair

options.label: B
options.text: Increasing the dryer's temperature so the hair dries faster

options.label: C
options.text: Concentrating airflow into a single, powerful jet

options.label: D
options.text: Smoothing the cuticle flat on straight hair for extra shine

questions.correct_answer_text: Spreading airflow gently, ideal for curly hair
questions.explanation: A diffuser disperses airflow over a wider, gentler area, commonly used on curly or textured hair to dry it with less frizz and better curl definition.

questions.question: According to the Red Seal standard, when are the rollers or clips removed from a dried wet set?

options.label: A
options.text: Before the hair is tested for dryness, so the base can be checked

options.label: B
options.text: After finishing spray has been applied to the whole set

options.label: C
options.text: After the hair has cooled, without disturbing the base

options.label: D
options.text: As soon as the hood dryer stops, while the hair is warm and pliable

questions.correct_answer_text: After the hair has cooled, without disturbing the base
questions.explanation: The Red Seal standard sets the order for a wet set: dry the hair, test it, then remove the tools after the hair cools without disturbing the base (D-9.04 'remove tools'; D-9.05 'remove clips').

questions.question: What is a key consideration when choosing round brush size for a blow-dry style?

options.label: A
options.text: Brush size affects drying speed, not the size of the curl

options.label: B
options.text: Brush size matters for the length of the hair, not the curl

options.label: C
options.text: Larger barrels create tighter curls because more hair is wrapped around them

options.label: D
options.text: Larger barrels build looser waves; smaller ones create tighter curl

questions.correct_answer_text: Larger barrels build looser waves; smaller ones create tighter curl
questions.explanation: Round brush diameter directly affects the finished shape — larger brushes produce looser waves and volume, smaller brushes create tighter curls or more defined ends.

questions.question: A client's hair is already weakened from recent chemical services. What might excessive tension while blow-drying or brushing cause?

options.label: A
options.text: Improved shine, with no added risk to the hair

options.label: B
options.text: A temporary boost in shine that fades after washing

options.label: C
options.text: A longer-lasting style, since tension sets the hair

options.label: D
options.text: An increased risk of breakage and split ends

questions.correct_answer_text: An increased risk of breakage and split ends
questions.explanation: Applying excessive pulling tension to hair that is already weak or over-processed increases the likelihood of breakage during styling.

questions.question: What is the general purpose of finishing products, such as hairspray or shine serum, at the end of a style?

options.label: A
options.text: Finishing products repair damage left by heat styling tools

options.label: B
options.text: They permanently set the hair's shape after heat styling

options.label: C
options.text: Helping lock in the finished shape and add a polished look

options.label: D
options.text: Finishing products replace the need for heat protectant

questions.correct_answer_text: Helping lock in the finished shape and add a polished look
questions.explanation: Finishing products typically help hold the completed style in place and add a polished visual finish, complementing rather than replacing the styling work already done.

questions.question: Why check a flat iron's plates are clean before using it on a client?

options.label: A
options.text: Buildup can transfer to the hair and cause uneven results

options.label: B
options.text: The plates clean themselves once they reach operating temperature

options.label: C
options.text: Product residue on the plates helps the iron glide and protects the hair

options.label: D
options.text: Plate cleanliness affects heating speed but not the finished hair

questions.correct_answer_text: Buildup can transfer to the hair and cause uneven results
questions.explanation: Residue buildup on flat iron plates can transfer onto the client's hair and reduce even heat distribution, affecting the smoothness of the result.

questions.question: A client is attending an outdoor event in humid weather. What styling factor matters most for their finished look?

options.label: A
options.text: Using humidity-resistant products so the style holds longer

options.label: B
options.text: Humidity affects hair that is chemically relaxed, not natural hair

options.label: C
options.text: Humidity affects the hair's colour, not the style

options.label: D
options.text: Technique stays the same in any weather; the product amount changes

questions.correct_answer_text: Using humidity-resistant products so the style holds longer
questions.explanation: Humidity can cause styled hair to lose shape or frizz more quickly, so choosing humidity-resistant products and techniques helps a style last longer outdoors.

questions.question: Why is a heat-protectant and smoothing routine important before flat-ironing textured or coily hair for a straightened result?

options.label: A
options.text: Repeated passes make the cuticle stronger with each pass

options.label: B
options.text: Heat protectant is unnecessary on textured or coily hair types

options.label: C
options.text: Smoothing routines are needed on chemically relaxed hair, not on natural coils

options.label: D
options.text: It protects against repeated high-heat passes often needed for smoothness

questions.correct_answer_text: It protects against repeated high-heat passes often needed for smoothness
questions.explanation: Textured or coily hair being straightened often needs more heat passes to achieve smoothness, making heat protection and proper prep especially important to limit cumulative damage.

questions.question: Which product is worked through damp hair before finger waves are shaped?

options.label: A
options.text: A leave-in heat-protectant spray

options.label: B
options.text: A setting lotion or finger-wave gel

options.label: C
options.text: A silicone serum for easy combing

options.label: D
options.text: A dry shampoo, to give the hair grip

questions.correct_answer_text: A setting lotion or finger-wave gel
questions.explanation: A setting lotion or gel gives the damp hair hold and slip, so the ridges can be moulded with the fingers and comb and will dry in shape.

questions.question: Which description matches a finger wave?

options.label: A
options.text: Alternating C-shaped waves moulded into wet hair with only the fingers and a comb

options.label: B
options.text: Tight circular curls pinned flat against the scalp

options.label: C
options.text: Alternating C-shaped waves pressed into dry hair with a flat iron

options.label: D
options.text: Uniform spiral curls wound around rods on damp hair

questions.correct_answer_text: Alternating C-shaped waves moulded into wet hair with only the fingers and a comb
questions.explanation: The Red Seal glossary defines a finger wave as alternating C-shaped waves made by shaping and moulding wet hair using only the fingers and a comb, and the STO glossary adds that no heat is used. Spirals wound on rods belong to a perm or wave, and circular curls pinned flat are pin curls.

questions.question: In hair styling, what does 'base control' refer to?

options.label: A
options.text: The amount of tension used when combing the hair over the tool

options.label: B
options.text: The order in which the sections are set on the head

options.label: C
options.text: The diameter of the tool chosen for the curl wanted

options.label: D
options.text: The position of the tool in relation to the base

questions.correct_answer_text: The position of the tool in relation to the base
questions.explanation: The STO glossary defines base control as the position of the tool in relation to the base, and unit 8.5 has apprentices define the three base controls (on base, off base and half base) and describe the volume each one gives. Tension, section order and tool size are separate decisions in a set.

questions.question: Which safety practice protects the client's scalp when a thermal tool is used close to the roots?

options.label: A
options.text: Holding the tool at a 90-degree angle to the head

options.label: B
options.text: Placing a comb between the tool and the scalp

options.label: C
options.text: Applying a protective base cream to the scalp first

options.label: D
options.text: Setting the tool to maximum so it passes quickly

questions.correct_answer_text: Placing a comb between the tool and the scalp
questions.explanation: A comb placed between the hot barrel or plate and the scalp acts as a shield. The stylist also tests the tool's temperature before use and keeps the cord in good condition.

questions.question: How should a stylist direct the airflow of a hair dryer to protect the client's scalp?

options.label: A
options.text: Straight at the roots, to speed drying where the hair is thickest

options.label: B
options.text: Directly at the nape, since the skin there tolerates heat

options.label: C
options.text: Toward the scalp, with the dryer held close for control

options.label: D
options.text: Away from the scalp, along the hair shaft, keeping the dryer moving

questions.correct_answer_text: Away from the scalp, along the hair shaft, keeping the dryer moving
questions.explanation: Airflow is directed away from the scalp and along the hair shaft. The temperature is adjusted for the hair, and the dryer is kept at a safe distance from the hair and moving, so no area overheats.

questions.question: What type of bond within the cortex is mainly altered during a permanent wave or relaxing service?

options.label: A
options.text: Disulfide bonds

options.label: B
options.text: Hydrogen bonds

options.label: C
options.text: Bonds inside the hair's pigment granules

options.label: D
options.text: Peptide bonds along the keratin chains

questions.correct_answer_text: Disulfide bonds
questions.explanation: Permanent waving and relaxing chemically break and reform disulfide bonds, strong sulfur-sulfur bonds within the cortex, which allows a lasting change to the hair's curl or straightness.

questions.question: Under Health Canada's Cosmetic Ingredient Hotlist, what is the limit for thioglycolic acid in professional-use hair waving products?

options.label: A
options.text: 8% (as thioglycolic acid) with a pH of 9.5 or less

options.label: B
options.text: 11% (as thioglycolic acid) with a pH of 12.7 or less

options.label: C
options.text: 5% (as thioglycolic acid) with a pH of 12.7 or less

options.label: D
options.text: 11% (as thioglycolic acid) with a pH of 9.5 or less

questions.correct_answer_text: 11% (as thioglycolic acid) with a pH of 9.5 or less
questions.explanation: The Hotlist restricts thioglycolic acid and its salts in professional hair dyes, waving or straightening products to 11% (as thioglycolic acid) with a pH of 9.5 or less. The 8% limit is the general-use limit for the same products, and 5% with a pH of 12.7 or less applies to depilatories.

questions.question: What is the role of the neutralizer in a permanent waving service?

options.label: A
options.text: Stripping all pigment from the hair strand

options.label: B
options.text: Permanently softening the hair's overall texture

options.label: C
options.text: Reforming broken disulfide bonds in the new shape

options.label: D
options.text: Raising the pH so the hair swells before it is waved

questions.correct_answer_text: Reforming broken disulfide bonds in the new shape
questions.explanation: The neutralizer, an oxidizing step, rebuilds the disulfide bonds broken by the waving lotion, locking the hair into its new curl pattern around the rods.

questions.question: A client asks whether a hydroxide relaxer and a thio-based product can both be used on their hair the same day. What should the stylist explain?

options.label: A
options.text: Combining them can cause severe, unpredictable damage or breakage

options.label: B
options.text: Combining them produces a stronger, more reliable result

options.label: C
options.text: The restriction applies to hair that is already coloured

options.label: D
options.text: Combining them is safe if the second service is applied within an hour

questions.correct_answer_text: Combining them can cause severe, unpredictable damage or breakage
questions.explanation: Hydroxide and thio chemistries act very differently on the hair's bonds; combining them risks severe structural damage, so professional guidance strongly warns against using both on the same head at once.

questions.question: A chemical product is described as alkaline. What does the 332A curriculum glossary say that means for its pH?

options.label: A
options.text: Its pH is exactly 7.0

options.label: B
options.text: Its pH is between 4.5 and 5.5, like the scalp

options.label: C
options.text: Its pH is below 7.0

options.label: D
options.text: Its pH is greater than 7.0

questions.correct_answer_text: Its pH is greater than 7.0
questions.explanation: The glossary defines alkaline as having a pH of greater than 7.0, and acidity as a pH below 7.0; its pH entry places 7 through 14 on the alkaline side of the scale.

questions.question: Why is a strand test especially important before a first-time relaxer or perm service?

options.label: A
options.text: A strand test is done to check the client's skin for an allergic reaction

options.label: B
options.text: They replace the need to analyze porosity and elasticity

options.label: C
options.text: Strand tests are useful for colour services, not texture services

options.label: D
options.text: It helps predict processing time and reduce over-processing risk

questions.correct_answer_text: It helps predict processing time and reduce over-processing risk
questions.explanation: A strand test on unfamiliar hair helps the stylist estimate how it will respond to a specific chemical formula and timing before committing the whole head to the service.

questions.question: What does 'virgin hair' mean in the context of a chemical service?

options.label: A
options.text: Hair that has not been cut for a year or more

options.label: B
options.text: Hair that has never been chemically treated before

options.label: C
options.text: Hair belonging to a client who has not visited the salon before

options.label: D
options.text: Hair that has not been exposed to heat styling tools

questions.correct_answer_text: Hair that has never been chemically treated before
questions.explanation: 'Virgin hair' refers to hair with no prior chemical processing, such as colour, perm, or relaxer, which affects how it may respond compared to previously treated hair.

questions.question: A client returns for a relaxer re-touch. Why should the stylist avoid overlapping previously relaxed hair with fresh product?

options.label: A
options.text: Overlapping strengthens the results of the previous service

options.label: B
options.text: Overlapping saves time because the head does not need to be sectioned

options.label: C
options.text: Overlap is needed so the relaxer line cannot be seen at the regrowth

options.label: D
options.text: Overlapping already-processed hair risks over-processing and breakage

questions.correct_answer_text: Overlapping already-processed hair risks over-processing and breakage
questions.explanation: Re-touch applications should mainly target new growth; applying strong chemical over already-processed lengths again increases the risk of over-processing and breakage.

questions.question: What does developer, or hydrogen peroxide, volume generally control in an oxidative chemical process?

options.label: A
options.text: The scent and fragrance strength of the finished product

options.label: B
options.text: Whether the product is classed as permanent or semi-permanent

options.label: C
options.text: How long the product can be stored once it is opened

options.label: D
options.text: The strength of lift, with higher volumes lifting more

questions.correct_answer_text: The strength of lift, with higher volumes lifting more
questions.explanation: Developer volume, such as 10, 20, 30, or 40, affects the degree of lift or lightening an oxidative colour or lightener can achieve, though higher volumes also carry greater risk.

questions.question: What does a test curl determine during a permanent wave service?

options.label: A
options.text: How long a colour formula should stay on the hair

options.label: B
options.text: How the hair reacts to the waving solution, shown by the curl formed

options.label: C
options.text: Whether the client is allergic to the waving solution

options.label: D
options.text: Whether the neutralizer has been rinsed out completely

questions.correct_answer_text: How the hair reacts to the waving solution, shown by the curl formed
questions.explanation: The Red Seal glossary defines a test curl as the process used to determine the hair's reaction to permanent wave solution in order to achieve the desired result, and the STO glossary adds that it checks curl formation during the wave. Allergy checks are patch tests, and a colour formula's timing comes from a strand test.

questions.question: Why do higher developer volumes, such as 40 volume, generally carry greater risk to hair and scalp than lower volumes?

options.label: A
options.text: Volume controls the final shade of colour, not the risk of damage

options.label: B
options.text: The risk depends on the colour brand, not on the developer volume

options.label: C
options.text: They are stronger oxidizers, with more lift and damage risk

options.label: D
options.text: Higher volumes are actually gentler on the hair overall

questions.correct_answer_text: They are stronger oxidizers, with more lift and damage risk
questions.explanation: Higher-volume developers are stronger oxidizing agents capable of greater lightening action, which also raises the potential for hair damage or scalp irritation if used carelessly.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a patch test before certain chemical services, particularly some colour products?

options.label: A
options.text: Checking for a skin allergic reaction before full application

options.label: B
options.text: Checking the client's overall hair porosity level

options.label: C
options.text: Testing the final expected colour result on the hair

options.label: D
options.text: Checking the strength of developer needed for the client's hair

questions.correct_answer_text: Checking for a skin allergic reaction before full application
questions.explanation: A patch test applies a small amount of product to skin in advance, checking for allergic sensitivity before it is used more broadly on the scalp and hair.

questions.question: What might a positive, reactive patch test result indicate?

options.label: A
options.text: The test itself was performed incorrectly and should be disregarded

options.label: B
options.text: The client's hair has excellent porosity for the planned service

options.label: C
options.text: The product is particularly well-suited to that client

options.label: D
options.text: A possible allergy to an ingredient, meaning it should not be used

questions.correct_answer_text: A possible allergy to an ingredient, meaning it should not be used
questions.explanation: A positive or reactive patch test result signals a possible allergic sensitivity, meaning that specific product formula should not be used on that client.

questions.question: Why does hair porosity matter when choosing processing time for a chemical relaxer or perm?

options.label: A
options.text: Higher porosity hair often processes faster, needing shorter timing

options.label: B
options.text: Lower porosity hair processes faster because its cuticle lies tighter

options.label: C
options.text: Porosity affects the finished shade rather than processing time

options.label: D
options.text: Processing time is identical whatever the porosity

questions.correct_answer_text: Higher porosity hair often processes faster, needing shorter timing
questions.explanation: More porous hair generally absorbs chemicals faster, which can mean shorter safe processing times are needed to avoid over-processing and damage.

questions.question: What is a key risk of over-processing during a chemical relaxer service?

options.label: A
options.text: Over-processing dries hair temporarily, then it recovers

options.label: B
options.text: It changes the hair's colour but not its strength

options.label: C
options.text: Excessive breakage or severe structural damage to the hair

options.label: D
options.text: It results in shinier hair that is notably stronger

questions.correct_answer_text: Excessive breakage or severe structural damage to the hair
questions.explanation: Leaving a chemical relaxer on beyond the appropriate time for that hair's condition and porosity significantly raises the risk of severe breakage and structural damage.

questions.question: What does 'base' application typically refer to in relaxer terminology?

options.label: A
options.text: The neutralizing step that follows the final rinse

options.label: B
options.text: Applying a protective cream to the scalp before the relaxer

options.label: C
options.text: A term that applies to acid perms, not to relaxers

options.label: D
options.text: Applying relaxer to the hair ends, skipping the roots

questions.correct_answer_text: Applying a protective cream to the scalp before the relaxer
questions.explanation: A 'base' relaxer is one that requires a protective base cream to be applied to the scalp before the relaxer, in contrast to 'no-base' formulas that have the protective barrier built in.

questions.question: What does 'processing time' refer to in a chemical texture service?

options.label: A
options.text: The time a chemical product stays on hair to take effect

options.label: B
options.text: The time needed to clean the salon workstation afterward

options.label: C
options.text: The time the stylist spends rinsing the product from the hair

options.label: D
options.text: The time it takes to book the client's appointment

questions.correct_answer_text: The time a chemical product stays on hair to take effect
questions.explanation: Processing time is the duration a chemical formula, such as a relaxer, perm, or colour, remains on hair to achieve its intended change before being rinsed or neutralized.

questions.question: Why is timing especially critical during the neutralizing step of a permanent wave?

options.label: A
options.text: Neutralizer timing changes the hair colour more than the curl

options.label: B
options.text: A longer neutralizing time is better than the labelled time

options.label: C
options.text: Neutralizer timing matters for the first rod, not for the rest of the head

options.label: D
options.text: Insufficient time can leave bonds incompletely reformed, risking a weak curl

questions.correct_answer_text: Insufficient time can leave bonds incompletely reformed, risking a weak curl
questions.explanation: The neutralizer needs enough contact time to properly reform disulfide bonds; cutting this step short can leave a weak, unstable, or quickly relaxing curl.

questions.question: Why is it generally inadvisable to relax or perm hair that is already significantly damaged, with very low elasticity?

options.label: A
options.text: Elasticity is tested after the service to confirm the result

options.label: B
options.text: Damaged hair carries no additional risk compared to healthy hair

options.label: C
options.text: Damaged hair absorbs the chemical evenly, so it tolerates it better than healthy hair

options.label: D
options.text: It may not safely tolerate additional chemical stress and could break

questions.correct_answer_text: It may not safely tolerate additional chemical stress and could break
questions.explanation: Weak, low-elasticity hair has reduced structural reserve, so additional chemical stress from a relaxer or perm significantly raises the risk of breakage or hair loss.

questions.question: What is a general purpose of a conditioning treatment recommended after a chemical texture service?

options.label: A
options.text: Helping restore moisture and support the newly altered hair structure

options.label: B
options.text: Reversing the chemical change so the hair returns to its natural texture

options.label: C
options.text: Conditioning is used to seal the neutralizer inside the hair

options.label: D
options.text: Conditioning is needed after a relaxer, not after a perm

questions.correct_answer_text: Helping restore moisture and support the newly altered hair structure
questions.explanation: Post-service conditioning helps replenish moisture and support the hair's now-altered internal structure, improving manageability without undoing the intended chemical change.

questions.question: What is a self-activating (exothermic) permanent wave?

options.label: A
options.text: A perm whose chemicals release heat to form the curls

options.label: B
options.text: A perm that processes at room temperature with no neutralizer

options.label: C
options.text: A perm activated by adding an alkaline booster to the solution just before use

options.label: D
options.text: A perm that needs a thermal processing accelerator to supply heat

questions.correct_answer_text: A perm whose chemicals release heat to form the curls
questions.explanation: The STO glossary defines a self-activating wave as a permanent wave using chemicals that release heat to create curls. An accelerator is separate equipment that supplies heat, and an activator is an additive that quickens the action of a chemical.

questions.question: Why is a cotton coil placed around the hairline before waving solution is applied?

options.label: A
options.text: To neutralize the solution before it reaches the skin

options.label: B
options.text: To hold the rods in place while they process

options.label: C
options.text: To absorb solution that runs and keep it off the skin

options.label: D
options.text: To keep the client's body heat on the scalp during processing

questions.correct_answer_text: To absorb solution that runs and keep it off the skin
questions.explanation: Cotton secured at the hairline, together with a protective cream, absorbs solution that runs and keeps it off the client's skin and eyes. Damp cotton is replaced as needed.

questions.question: Which active ingredient defines a 'lye' relaxer?

options.label: A
options.text: Hydrogen peroxide

options.label: B
options.text: Guanidine hydroxide

options.label: C
options.text: Ammonium thioglycolate

options.label: D
options.text: Sodium hydroxide

questions.correct_answer_text: Sodium hydroxide
questions.explanation: Lye relaxers use sodium hydroxide. No-lye relaxers use guanidine hydroxide, and thio relaxers use ammonium thioglycolate, a reducing agent. Hydrogen peroxide is the oxidizer in colour and lightener developers.

questions.question: What is the job of the neutralizing step after a hydroxide relaxer has been rinsed out?

options.label: A
options.text: To lighten the hair so it matches the regrowth

options.label: B
options.text: To rebuild the disulfide bonds in their new straight shape

options.label: C
options.text: To leave a protective base cream on the scalp for the next service

options.label: D
options.text: To stop the relaxing action and return the hair to its natural pH

questions.correct_answer_text: To stop the relaxing action and return the hair to its natural pH
questions.explanation: After the rinse, a neutralizing shampoo or pH reducer stops the relaxing action, removes alkaline residue and returns the hair and scalp to their natural acidic pH, which also closes the cuticle. A hydroxide relaxer does not need the bond-reforming oxidizer that a perm uses.

questions.question: Which list names the categories used to classify hair colour products by how long they last?

options.label: A
options.text: Vegetable, mineral, and synthetic

options.label: B
options.text: Temporary, semi-permanent, demi-permanent, and permanent

options.label: C
options.text: Warm, cool, and neutral

options.label: D
options.text: Oxidative, non-oxidative, and metallic

questions.correct_answer_text: Temporary, semi-permanent, demi-permanent, and permanent
questions.explanation: Hair colour products are grouped by longevity into temporary (surface coating, removed by shampooing), semi-permanent (partial penetration, fades with washing), demi-permanent (low-volume developer, no significant lift) and permanent (chemical change that lasts until new growth).

questions.question: What does 'level' refer to in a hair colour system?

options.label: A
options.text: The amount of warmth in a colour, from gold to ash

options.label: B
options.text: The lightness or darkness of a colour, on a numbered scale

options.label: C
options.text: The acidity of the colour mixture, measured on the pH scale

options.label: D
options.text: The strength of the developer used in the mixture

questions.correct_answer_text: The lightness or darkness of a colour, on a numbered scale
questions.explanation: Level describes how light or dark a hair colour is, usually expressed on a standardized numerical scale, such as 1 for black through 10 for the lightest blonde.

questions.question: What does 'tone' refer to in hair colour terminology?

options.label: A
options.text: The developer volume selected for the service

options.label: B
options.text: The level or lightness of a colour, considered on its own

options.label: C
options.text: The warmth or coolness of a colour, such as gold or ash

options.label: D
options.text: The processing time required by a particular formula

questions.correct_answer_text: The warmth or coolness of a colour, such as gold or ash
questions.explanation: Tone describes the warm, such as gold, red, or orange, or cool, such as ash or violet, quality of a colour, distinct from level, which measures lightness or darkness.

questions.question: What is the general purpose of a lightener, or bleach, product?

options.label: A
options.text: Adding shine and tone without changing the hair's level

options.label: B
options.text: Oxidizing and removing pigment from hair, raising its level

options.label: C
options.text: Depositing permanent artificial pigment into the hair shaft

options.label: D
options.text: Lowering the hair's level, making it appear darker

questions.correct_answer_text: Oxidizing and removing pigment from hair, raising its level
questions.explanation: Lighteners work by oxidizing and breaking down melanin, and sometimes artificial pigment, within the hair, raising its level and making it lighter.

questions.question: What does 'underlying pigment,' sometimes called contributing pigment, refer to when lightening hair?

options.label: A
options.text: The colour of the developer once it is mixed with lightener

options.label: B
options.text: A synthetic dye added at the final stage to correct the tone

options.label: C
options.text: The natural warm tones exposed as hair is progressively lightened

options.label: D
options.text: The shade of toner chosen to counteract the lightener

questions.correct_answer_text: The natural warm tones exposed as hair is progressively lightened
questions.explanation: As hair lightens, natural pigments are exposed progressively, typically moving through red, orange, and yellow tones before reaching the palest levels — this progression is the underlying pigment.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a toner applied after lightening hair?

options.label: A
options.text: Closing the cuticle so the lightener cannot lift any further

options.label: B
options.text: Neutralizing unwanted warm tones and refining the final shade

options.label: C
options.text: Further lightening the hair beyond the initial lightening step

options.label: D
options.text: Permanently strengthening the hair's internal bonds

questions.correct_answer_text: Neutralizing unwanted warm tones and refining the final shade
questions.explanation: A toner, often a demi- or semi-permanent colour, is used after lightening to neutralize unwanted warmth and achieve the desired final shade.

questions.question: Under standard colour theory used in hairstyling, which colour neutralizes orange tones?

options.label: A
options.text: Yellow

options.label: B
options.text: Blue

options.label: C
options.text: Red

options.label: D
options.text: Green

questions.correct_answer_text: Blue
questions.explanation: Colours opposite each other on the colour wheel neutralize one another; blue sits opposite orange, which is why blue-based toners counteract orange or brassy tones.

questions.question: Which colour is typically used to neutralize unwanted yellow tones in lightened hair?

options.label: A
options.text: Green

options.label: B
options.text: Violet or purple

options.label: C
options.text: Red

options.label: D
options.text: Orange

questions.correct_answer_text: Violet or purple
questions.explanation: Violet sits opposite yellow on the colour wheel, which is why purple-based toning shampoos and toners are commonly used to counteract unwanted yellow or brassy tones.

questions.question: A returning client books a colour retouch. Why does this service typically focus on new growth rather than the full length?

options.label: A
options.text: Previously coloured lengths can be damaged at full strength

options.label: B
options.text: The regrowth is the same shade as the previously coloured lengths

options.label: C
options.text: Retouches are applied to the very ends of the hair

options.label: D
options.text: Retouches cover the entire head with fresh product

questions.correct_answer_text: Previously coloured lengths can be damaged at full strength
questions.explanation: A retouch targets new growth at the root, since the remaining length has already absorbed colour previously — reprocessing it with full-strength product risks damage or buildup.

questions.question: What does 'colour correction' generally refer to in a salon context?

options.label: A
options.text: Matching a client's skin tone to the best shade on a colour chart

options.label: B
options.text: A specialized process fixing an undesired or uneven prior result

options.label: C
options.text: A synonym for a basic, single-process colour service

options.label: D
options.text: A routine root retouch performed on a regular schedule

questions.correct_answer_text: A specialized process fixing an undesired or uneven prior result
questions.explanation: Colour correction refers to the more advanced process of diagnosing and fixing an unwanted or uneven prior colour result, often needing multiple steps and careful planning.

questions.question: A client requests a dramatic colour correction, such as going from very dark to very light. Why might a stylist run a test or extended consultation first?

options.label: A
options.text: Consultation is unnecessary for colour correction work

options.label: B
options.text: Dramatic corrections are safely achievable in a single visit

options.label: C
options.text: To assess feasibility and damage risk, possibly across sessions

options.label: D
options.text: To confirm which retail products the client already owns

questions.correct_answer_text: To assess feasibility and damage risk, possibly across sessions
questions.explanation: Major colour corrections can carry significant risk of damage; assessing hair condition and planning, sometimes across multiple sessions, helps achieve the goal as safely as possible.

questions.question: What does 'double-process colour' typically refer to?

options.label: A
options.text: Applying permanent colour with two different developer volumes at once

options.label: B
options.text: Applying the exact same colour formula twice in a row

options.label: C
options.text: Two steps, usually lightening followed by toning or colour

options.label: D
options.text: A synonym for a routine retouch of the regrowth at the roots

questions.correct_answer_text: Two steps, usually lightening followed by toning or colour
questions.explanation: Double-process colour involves two distinct steps, most commonly lightening the hair first and then applying a toner or additional colour to reach the final shade.

questions.question: What is a general risk of combining lightening with a relaxer or perm too close together without proper spacing or testing?

options.label: A
options.text: Combining them evens out porosity, so the results improve with no added risk

options.label: B
options.text: Lightening strengthens hair against further chemical stress

options.label: C
options.text: Increased risk of severe damage from cumulative chemical stress

options.label: D
options.text: The two services cancel out each other's effects on the hair

questions.correct_answer_text: Increased risk of severe damage from cumulative chemical stress
questions.explanation: Lightening chemically weakens hair's structure, so layering another strong chemical process too soon, or without careful testing, greatly increases the risk of severe damage.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a gloss or glaze service often offered after colour or lightening?

options.label: A
options.text: Permanently lightening the hair further than before

options.label: B
options.text: Adding shine, refining tone, and boosting vibrancy

options.label: C
options.text: Removing artificial pigment so the hair returns to its natural level

options.label: D
options.text: Replacing the need for regular colour maintenance

questions.correct_answer_text: Adding shine, refining tone, and boosting vibrancy
questions.explanation: A gloss or glaze is typically a lower-commitment, shine-boosting treatment that can refine tone and help maintain the colour's vibrancy between fuller colour services.

questions.question: Why consider a client's skin tone alongside their hair colour preference during a consultation?

options.label: A
options.text: Some tones may complement or clash with the complexion

options.label: B
options.text: Skin tone affects the haircut shape rather than the colour choice

options.label: C
options.text: Most colours read the same visually, whatever the skin tone

options.label: D
options.text: Skin tone matters for makeup choices, not for hair colour choices

questions.correct_answer_text: Some tones may complement or clash with the complexion
questions.explanation: Skin undertone can affect how a hair colour reads visually against the complexion, so many stylists factor it into recommending flattering colour and tone choices.

questions.question: What does 'resistant' hair mean in the context of colour services?

options.label: A
options.text: Hair that cannot be coloured under any circumstances

options.label: B
options.text: Hair that has taken on the same shade from repeated colouring

options.label: C
options.text: Hair with a tight cuticle that takes colour slowly

options.label: D
options.text: Hair with an unusually open cuticle and high porosity

questions.correct_answer_text: Hair with a tight cuticle that takes colour slowly
questions.explanation: Resistant hair has a tight cuticle structure that slows colour absorption, sometimes requiring pre-softening or longer processing time for even results.

questions.question: A client's hair is damaged and previously lightened, and now wants a different target shade applied over it. Why might the stylist perform a colour fill first?

options.label: A
options.text: A colour fill is applied to lighten hair that is too dark

options.label: B
options.text: A colour fill replaces the need for a final colour step

options.label: C
options.text: To restore lost pigment and create an even base for colour

options.label: D
options.text: Colour fills are meant for virgin hair with no prior colour

questions.correct_answer_text: To restore lost pigment and create an even base for colour
questions.explanation: A colour fill helps replace pigment in overly lightened or porous hair, creating a more even base tone so subsequent colour develops more predictably.

questions.question: Why does semi-permanent colour typically fade faster than permanent colour?

options.label: A
options.text: Semi-permanent colour contains a stronger developer that wears off

options.label: B
options.text: It doesn't rely on an oxidative developer to permanently alter the hair

options.label: C
options.text: Permanent colour fades at the same rate because both use the same pigment

options.label: D
options.text: It sits on the surface of the cuticle, so it rubs off like a temporary rinse

questions.correct_answer_text: It doesn't rely on an oxidative developer to permanently alter the hair
questions.explanation: Semi-permanent colour typically deposits pigment without a developer causing a permanent chemical change, so it gradually fades with washing rather than growing out like permanent colour.

questions.question: Why is even, methodical application important during a full-head lightening service?

options.label: A
options.text: Lightener spreads itself evenly once the cap is on, so application can be quick

options.label: B
options.text: Application technique affects the shade, not the evenness of lift

options.label: C
options.text: Uneven timing or application can cause blotchy, inconsistent lightening

options.label: D
options.text: Lightener processes at the same speed over the whole head, so technique does not matter

questions.correct_answer_text: Uneven timing or application can cause blotchy, inconsistent lightening
questions.explanation: Careful, consistent application and timing across sections helps avoid patchy or uneven lightening, since factors like scalp heat and product exposure time vary by area.

questions.question: A strand test shows a planned colour or lightening service is likely to cause excessive damage. What is the reasonable response?

options.label: A
options.text: Proceed with the original plan but cut the processing time in half

options.label: B
options.text: Disregard strand test results, since they cannot predict the full-head result

options.label: C
options.text: Treat the result as inconclusive and repeat the strand test unchanged

options.label: D
options.text: Discuss the risk honestly and recommend a safer alternative plan

questions.correct_answer_text: Discuss the risk honestly and recommend a safer alternative plan
questions.explanation: A strand test showing likely excessive damage is exactly the situation it's meant to catch — the professional response is honest communication and adjusting the plan for safety.

questions.question: In the 332A curriculum glossary, what does 'lift' mean in colour work?

options.label: A
options.text: The ability of a colour product to add pigment to the hair

options.label: B
options.text: The process of lightening existing colour

options.label: C
options.text: The degree of lightness or darkness of the hair colour

options.label: D
options.text: The warmth or coolness of a colour

questions.correct_answer_text: The process of lightening existing colour
questions.explanation: The glossary defines lift as the process of lightening existing colour. Adding pigment is colour deposit, warmth or coolness is tone, and the lightness or darkness of hair colour is its level.

questions.question: Under Health Canada's Cosmetic Ingredient Hotlist, what is the maximum concentration of hydrogen peroxide in hair products?

options.label: A
options.text: 6% (as applied)

options.label: B
options.text: 3% (as applied)

options.label: C
options.text: 10% (as applied)

options.label: D
options.text: 12% (as applied)

questions.correct_answer_text: 10% (as applied)
questions.explanation: The Hotlist lists peroxide and peroxide-generating compounds as restricted and sets a limit of 10% (as applied) for hair products. 'As applied' refers to the product as it is used on the hair.

questions.question: Which colours are the primary colours in hair colour theory?

options.label: A
options.text: Orange, green and violet

options.label: B
options.text: Yellow, orange and red

options.label: C
options.text: Red, yellow and blue

options.label: D
options.text: Red, green and blue

questions.correct_answer_text: Red, yellow and blue
questions.explanation: The primary colours are red, yellow and blue. Mixing two primaries makes a secondary colour (orange, green or violet). Orange, green and violet are the secondary colours, and each secondary neutralizes the primary opposite it on the colour wheel.

questions.question: According to Health Canada, how is a skin patch test for hair dye done?

options.label: A
options.text: A small amount is applied behind the ear or on the inner forearm and checked after 24 hours

options.label: B
options.text: A full-strength mix is applied to the nape and checked after the processing time

options.label: C
options.text: A small amount is applied to the palm and checked after 30 minutes

options.label: D
options.text: A small amount is applied to the scalp at the crown and rinsed off after five minutes

questions.correct_answer_text: A small amount is applied behind the ear or on the inner forearm and checked after 24 hours
questions.explanation: Health Canada's instructions for hair dyes call for a small amount to be put behind the ear or on the inner forearm and checked after 24 hours. Redness, burning, itching or blistering means the product must not be used, and the test is repeated before each use because sensitivity can develop over time.

questions.question: Why must a stylist not use ordinary permanent scalp hair dye on a client's eyebrows or eyelashes?

options.label: A
options.text: Brow hair is too fine for oxidative colour to develop evenly

options.label: B
options.text: The developer would lift the eyebrow hair out of the skin

options.label: C
options.text: Hair dye near the eyes can cause serious eye injury, including blindness

options.label: D
options.text: Eyebrow hair has no melanin, so colour cannot attach to it

questions.correct_answer_text: Hair dye near the eyes can cause serious eye injury, including blindness
questions.explanation: Health Canada requires permanent and semi-permanent hair dyes to carry a warning against use on eyebrows and eyelashes, because getting dye in the eye can cause serious injury, including blindness. Facial hair colouring is done with products and methods made for it.

questions.question: What is a key maintenance difference between human-hair and synthetic wigs?

options.label: A
options.text: Human-hair wigs cannot be washed and may be dry-cleaned

options.label: B
options.text: The two types have essentially identical maintenance needs

options.label: C
options.text: Human-hair wigs tolerate heat styling better than synthetics

options.label: D
options.text: Synthetic fibre takes permanent hair colour, but human hair cannot

questions.correct_answer_text: Human-hair wigs tolerate heat styling better than synthetics
questions.explanation: Human-hair wigs can generally be washed, coloured, and heat-styled much like natural hair with care, while standard synthetic fibers can melt or become damaged with regular heat tools.

questions.question: Why is properly measuring a client's head important before fitting a custom wig or hairpiece?

options.label: A
options.text: To ensure a secure, comfortable, and natural-looking fit

options.label: B
options.text: Measurements are needed for synthetic wigs, not human-hair ones

options.label: C
options.text: Measuring is done to choose the wig's colour rather than its fit

options.label: D
options.text: Measuring is done to decide the price of the finished wig

questions.correct_answer_text: To ensure a secure, comfortable, and natural-looking fit
questions.explanation: Accurate head measurements are essential for a wig or hairpiece to sit securely and naturally, avoiding slipping, discomfort, or an unnatural appearance.

questions.question: What is 'bonding' in the context of hair extensions?

options.label: A
options.text: Attaching extensions with an adhesive, sometimes heated

options.label: B
options.text: Attaching extensions with crimped micro-links and no adhesive

options.label: C
options.text: Sewing wefts onto a braided track with needle and thread

options.label: D
options.text: Clipping wefts into the hair with small metal clips

questions.correct_answer_text: Attaching extensions with an adhesive, sometimes heated
questions.explanation: Bonding attachment methods use an adhesive, sometimes heat-activated as with keratin or fusion bonds, to fuse extension strands to natural hair near the root.

questions.question: What is a 'sew-in,' or track, method of extension attachment?

options.label: A
options.text: Extensions bonded to the natural hair with keratin and a heated tool

options.label: B
options.text: Extensions glued directly onto strands with no braiding involved

options.label: C
options.text: Wefted extensions sewn onto natural hair braided into a track

options.label: D
options.text: A term for extensions held in place by small metal clips

questions.correct_answer_text: Wefted extensions sewn onto natural hair braided into a track
questions.explanation: In a sew-in, the natural hair is typically braided into a track, and wefted extensions are then sewn onto that braided foundation using needle and thread.

questions.question: How do tape-in extensions differ from fusion, or keratin bond, extensions in attachment method?

options.label: A
options.text: Fusion extensions are wefts sewn onto a braided track

options.label: B
options.text: The two methods are identical, marketed under different names

options.label: C
options.text: Tape-ins sandwich hair between wefts; fusion fuses strand by strand

options.label: D
options.text: Tape-ins are attached with a heated tool, while fusion uses adhesive strips

questions.correct_answer_text: Tape-ins sandwich hair between wefts; fusion fuses strand by strand
questions.explanation: Tape-in extensions sandwich small natural hair sections between two adhesive-backed wefts, while fusion/keratin-bond extensions attach strand by strand using a heated tool to melt a bond onto the hair.

questions.question: A client with fine, low-density hair asks about heavier bonded extensions. Why should the stylist consider their natural hair health first?

options.label: A
options.text: Density matters for choosing the extension colour, not the method

options.label: B
options.text: All extension methods are equally safe on any hair type

options.label: C
options.text: Extension method affects the price but not natural hair health

options.label: D
options.text: Excess weight or tension on fragile hair can cause traction damage

questions.correct_answer_text: Excess weight or tension on fragile hair can cause traction damage
questions.explanation: Some attachment methods add more weight or root tension than fine, thin, or fragile natural hair can safely support, risking traction alopecia or breakage.

questions.question: What does 'traction alopecia' refer to, relevant to extension and tight-style safety?

options.label: A
options.text: Hair loss caused by repeated or prolonged tension

options.label: B
options.text: Patchy hair loss caused by an autoimmune condition

options.label: C
options.text: Hair loss caused by a fungal infection of the scalp

options.label: D
options.text: A term describing normal, expected seasonal shedding

questions.correct_answer_text: Hair loss caused by repeated or prolonged tension
questions.explanation: Traction alopecia is hair loss caused by sustained pulling tension on the follicle, a real risk with overly tight extensions, braids, or other high-tension styles.

questions.question: What is a general difference in washing products used for human-hair versus synthetic wigs?

options.label: A
options.text: Synthetic wigs are washed in hot water to restore their style

options.label: B
options.text: Human-hair wigs must be dry-cleaned because water damages the hair

options.label: C
options.text: Human-hair pieces generally use products similar to natural hair care

options.label: D
options.text: Both types need the same shampoo, conditioner, and washing method

questions.correct_answer_text: Human-hair pieces generally use products similar to natural hair care
questions.explanation: Synthetic wigs are typically cared for with products designed for synthetic fibers, while human-hair wigs can generally use products similar to those used on natural hair.

questions.question: A client is considering a long-term bonded extension method. Why might a stylist recommend a trial or thorough consultation first?

options.label: A
options.text: A trial lets the client keep the extensions free for a week

options.label: B
options.text: A consultation is skipped for bonded methods because the products are standard

options.label: C
options.text: To confirm the method suits the client's hair health and lifestyle

options.label: D
options.text: A trial lets the stylist skip the consultation on the day

questions.correct_answer_text: To confirm the method suits the client's hair health and lifestyle
questions.explanation: A trial or thorough consultation helps confirm the chosen extension method fits the client's hair health, lifestyle, and maintenance capability before a longer-term commitment.

questions.question: What maintenance consideration matters for bonded or fusion extensions as natural hair grows out?

questions.correct_answer_text: They generally need periodic reapplication closer to the scalp
questions.explanation: As natural hair grows, bonds move further from the scalp, so most bonded or fusion methods need periodic maintenance, removal, and reapplication closer to the scalp to stay secure.

questions.question: What do clip-in extensions generally offer compared to bonded or sewn-in methods?

questions.explanation: Clip-in extensions attach via small clips on wefts, offering a temporary option the client can put in and take out themselves, unlike more permanent bonded or sewn-in methods.
